title: University identity
content: OTH Amberg-Weiden is an applied sciences university in the Upper Palatinate, Bavaria. It operates main campuses in Amberg and Weiden, approximately 40 km apart. It has four faculties and practice-oriented programmes in engineering, IT, business and healthcare. Official institution name: Ostbayerische Technische Hochschule Amberg-Weiden. Do not confuse it with OTH Regensburg.

title: Faculties and distribution
content: The four faculties are Electrical Engineering, Media and Computer Science; Mechanical Engineering / Environmental Technology; Weiden Business School; and Industrial Engineering and Healthcare. The first two are primarily associated with Amberg and the latter two with Weiden. Individual programmes, modules and additional sites can differ: check programme pages.

title: Campus addresses
content: Weiden campus: Hetzenrichter Weg 15, 92637 Weiden, Germany. Amberg campus: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring 23, 92224 Amberg, Germany. The university main telephone listed is +49 (9621) 482-0. These are main campus addresses, not individual classroom locations.

title: Public versus authenticated information
content: The publicly accessible MyOTH landing page links to the noticeboard, PRIMUSS, Moodle, WebOPAC, email, registration and account tools. It does not make an individual person’s courses, grades, matriculation number, timetable or messages public. CampusOS must obtain a separately approved integration and appropriate permissions for any user-specific records.

title: Winter semester 2026/27
content: Official semester: 1 Oct 2026 - 14 Mar 2027. Teaching: 1 Oct 2026 - 15 Jan 2027 (regular lectures begin 2 Oct following first-year welcome). Exam registration: 9-17 Dec 2026; examinations: 16 Jan - 12 Feb 2027. Re-registration for the next semester: 14 Jan - 22 Feb 2027. The Christmas lecture-free period is 24 Dec 2026 - 6 Jan 2027. Dates should be confirmed at the official calendar prior to an action.

title: Summer semester 2027
content: Official semester: 15 Mar - 30 Sep 2027. Teaching: 15 Mar - 2 Jul 2027; examination registration: 19-27 May 2027; examinations: 3-30 Jul 2027; re-registration: 30 Jun - 11 Aug 2027. Multiple public-holiday lecture-free periods apply. Dates are time-sensitive and must be rechecked.

title: Exam and result procedures
content: PRIMUSS supports examination registration, grades, grade sheets, enrollment certificates and re-registration. For official deadlines or individual examination status, use PRIMUSS or current university announcements, not a cached answer in this PDF. The Students Office is responsible for academic administrative queries.

title: Programme directory: scope and use
content: The official online catalogue lists approximately 53 study-course entries across degree levels, fields, sites and formats as observed on 31 Oct 2026. This guide records 52 distinct representative catalogue names/variants; the list is not an authoritative enrollment or accreditation record. Check the live directory for current status, degree language, admission and campus.

title: Programme classification and matching
content: The catalogue supports filters for degree level, study format, admissions, starting term, course language, faculty, academic area and campus/location. A degree title by itself does not establish the programme’s current curriculum, teaching language, entry requirements or timetable. Career recommendations should link to the programme page and verify those attributes.

title: DTM headline facts
content: Digital Technology and Management (DTM) is an English-language B.Sc. based in Weiden with 7 standard semesters and 210 ECTS. It is listed in full-time and dual formats, with entry possible in winter or summer semester. It combines digital technology, computing, management, projects and intercultural skills.

title: DTM technical foundations
content: The published module structure includes Mathematics; Algorithms and Data Structures; Object-oriented Coding; Statistics and Quantitative Methods; Information Systems and Databases; and Research and Evaluation Methods. These modules build numerical, computing and applied research foundations. Exact assignments, module examinations and teaching terms must be checked in the current module handbook and applicable regulations.

title: DTM digital technology
content: The digital-technology area includes IoT Technology, Product Management, Sensors for Smart Systems, Communication Technology, Production Technology and Innovation and Technology Lifecycle Management. These combine technical systems knowledge with understanding the design and management of digital products.

title: DTM management and business
content: Management content includes Fundamentals of Business Administration; Principles of Accounting and Finance; Business Processes Management; Marketing and Sales; and Business Simulation. An AI learning assistant should distinguish official learning objectives from generic subject overviews when offering course-specific guidance.

title: DTM interdisciplinary work
content: Integrative modules include Project Management and Agile Methods, Logistics 1, Industrial Engineering, Ethics in Business and Technology, two Entrepreneurial Projects and a Research Project. These support project-based work, collaboration and business application of technical concepts.

title: DTM languages and practical phase
content: Language and soft-skill elements include English for Academic Purposes, Technical English, Intercultural Communication and basic elective options. The study structure also provides specialization electives, an internship and a bachelor thesis. Students should confirm the applicable semester plan for their entry cohort.

title: DTM module handbook: 2026/27
content: The current publicly linked DTM Course Catalogue is a 97-page PDF labelled Winter Term 2026/2027. It contains semester-plan variants and module descriptions, including learning objectives, content, credits, teaching modes and assessment forms. Some course-specific literature is accessible only through Moodle. The handbook distinguishes old versus newer examination regulations/cohorts; do not mix requirements.

title: DTM study regulations
content: The university publishes DTM programme/examination regulations, including an English consolidated translation of the first amendment dated 27 May 2024. The programme website explicitly warns that only the German legal text is binding. A CampusOS AI must not make authoritative legal or exam eligibility rulings using an English translation alone.

title: DTM admissions overview
content: The DTM application page lists an English B2 requirement and German A2 for applicants whose previous entrance qualification was not in German, subject to stated exceptions. The stated ordinary application periods are 15 Apr - 15 Jul for winter starts and 1 Nov - 15 Jan for summer starts, with exceptions possible. These requirements change, so verify live before advising an applicant.

title: DTM career and advising
content: DTM graduates can explore roles spanning digital product/project management, technical procurement, digital sales/after-sales and strategic business development across sectors such as industrial engineering and healthcare. The programme page gives dtm@oth-aw.de as a contact. These are examples of pathways, not job guarantees.

title: DTM document index
content: Official DTM structure page links winter- and summer-entry study plans, course catalogue/module handbook, examination schedule, regulations, presentation and flyer. Some linked timetables are explicitly labelled as old (e.g. a summer 2022 timetable); do not treat those as current. Use the 2026/27 course catalogue for currently published module descriptions and live portals for actual class schedules.

title: MyOTH as portal
content: MyOTH functions as a public entry point to university systems: Schwarzes Brett/noticeboard, PRIMUSS, Moodle, registration portals, library search, webmail, password management and university contact information. Many destination systems require university authentication. It is not itself a general-purpose public API exposing every student record.

title: Moodle
content: OTH uses Moodle for teaching and learning. Course spaces and materials may be visible only to enrolled/authorized users. CampusOS can link students to Moodle and, with institutional approval and scoped API permissions, retrieve course metadata or learning content. Do not scrape authenticated pages or store university passwords.

title: PRIMUSS
content: PRIMUSS is the university’s student administration portal for exam registration, certificates, grades and re-registration. This public reference does not include personal records. Linking to PRIMUSS is available; syncing data or taking actions would require explicit institutional authorization, user consent where applicable and audited permissions.

title: Noticeboard and campus announcements
content: The OTH online services directory describes the university noticeboard as a place for postponements, additional offers, university events and study information. CampusOS Connect can point students to this authoritative source, but must not treat unverified student posts as official university notices. Dynamic announcements need regular freshness checks.

title: OTH AW mobile app
content: The official OTH AW smartphone app includes access to news, timetables, room finding, library search, email, Moodle, PRIMUSS, campus dining, tasks, student ID and other features. CampusOS is a separate independent prototype, not a replacement or official integration unless OTH approves.

title: Roomfinder and IT tools
content: Online services provide a Roomfinder, student webmail and calendar tools, library databases/OPAC, Wi-Fi and VPN guidance, university GitLab, videoconferencing tools and printing services. Prefer linking users to the relevant official service rather than inventing room assignments or access instructions.

title: Library and e-resources
content: OTH has departmental libraries in both Amberg and Weiden. The public library page gives staffed opening hours and notes that eligible university members may gain 24-hour entry after chip-card activation and an introductory event; staffed hours and admission rules differ from 24-hour access. For book availability use the live OPAC.

title: Library contacts
content: Official library contact addresses listed: Amberg bibam@oth-aw.de; Weiden bibwen@oth-aw.de. During the semester, the page lists staffed hours Amberg Mon-Thu 09:00-17:00, Fri 09:00-14:00; Weiden Mon-Thu 08:00-17:00, Fri 08:00-14:00. Reconfirm holiday/semester-break schedules before recommending a visit.

title: Students Office / exam administration
content: The Students Office handles examination administration, online registration, records, academic recognition and administrative queries. Listed contact emails: Amberg studienbuero-am@oth-aw.de; Weiden studienbuero-wen@oth-aw.de. Exact office hours and faculty responsibilities should be checked on the current page.

title: International Office
content: The International Office supports international and exchange students and advises on study-related stays abroad. The public page asks visitors to arrange consultations by appointment and provides staff contacts and office hours. For visa/residence issues, the assistant should refer students to official immigration authorities and university support rather than giving individualized legal determinations.

title: Student advisory and degree contacts
content: The university provides a Student Advisory Service and programme-specific contacts through its official pages. Course/degree advice should use the applicable programme contacts and up-to-date regulation documents. Do not infer eligibility or exemptions from broad programme descriptions.

title: Weiden campus location and layout
content: Official Weiden campus address: Hetzenrichter Weg 15, 92637 Weiden. The published campus map labels the lecture hall building, Weiden Business School, Industrial Engineering and Healthcare faculty area (WIG), Mensa/Coffee Lounge, Weidener Technologie-Campus (WTC), E-House and Digital Business Campus. The map also indicates parking and assembly/AED points. Use the official map for directions.

title: Amberg campus location and layout
content: Official Amberg campus address: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring 23, 92224 Amberg. The published map labels faculty areas EMI and MB/UT, library, Mensa, administration, sports hall, Audimax/Siemens Innovatorium and parking. It also indicates assembly and AED points. This summary is a navigation index, not an indoor map or verified route plan.

title: Map and classroom limitations
content: The official campus PDFs are the authoritative visual reference for building positions. Neither a campus PDF nor a campus address gives live classroom schedules, accessibility routing, room occupancy or lecturer location. For a requested classroom (e.g. MF2), ask for or check a current Roomfinder/timetable record before giving a precise location.

title: Campus life and activities
content: OTH public campus-life pages point to dining, leisure/mobility activities, sport, cinema, choirs and university community offerings. Their availability depends on the term. CampusOS Connect may present verified events and opt-in recommendations, but should not invent dates or present unofficial events as institution-approved.

title: Marketplace, housing and student exchanges
content: The university marketplace provides accommodation listings, general offers/searches and a learning partner exchange. The main guidance names student residences in Weiden including Fischerberg and Postkeller. Advertisements are user-generated and can become outdated; CampusOS must verify current listing data before recommending a specific flat or job.

title: Jobs, projects and theses
content: University sources point to AViS for theses, pre-internships and internal student opportunities, a university vacancies page, a higher-education jobs marketplace, and student marketplace listings that sometimes include casual jobs. Vacancy details and deadlines are volatile. Only display a specific opening if it can be verified against a current authoritative listing.

title: Source hierarchy and legal caution
content: For questions on university rules, exam eligibility, programme-specific SPO or fees, prefer the current German legally binding regulation and live university notice. English translations, past-semester catalogues and summaries are supporting material, not binding authority. State relevant cohort and semester before applying a rule. Flag uncertainty rather than producing confident invented instructions.

title: Permissions and data boundaries
content: This PDF and JSONL only cover public university information. Do not claim knowledge of enrolled courses, student ID numbers, grades, attendance, lecturer calendars, Moodle private files, card/NFC mapping or building occupancy. Integrations require university approval, user authorization, audit trails, retention limits and role-based access controls.

title: Freshness and citation policy
content: Each answer should refer to its supporting source URL where feasible. Recheck time-sensitive matters: dates, exam timetables, fees, eligibility, staff, staff opening times, room assignments, job postings and social events. This knowledge snapshot was assembled on 31 Oct 2026 and is not auto-updating.

notes: Written from what the university site showed on 2026-11-08.
title: Where to find timetables, exam plans and old plans (Stundenpläne, Prüfungspläne, Archiv)
content: The current timetable (Stundenplan) and exam plan (Prüfungsplan) of every programme are listed by faculty on one page, "Stunden- und Prüfungspläne" / "Timetables and examination schedules". Each programme's own page also has them under Documents (Dokumente). The university replaces these files every semester, so older timetables and exam plans (old, previous, earlier semesters, archive, Archiv) are mostly no longer online; a few from 2024 and 2025 are still linked on programme pages. For an older plan, open the programme page and check its Documents, or ask the Studienbüro (study office). The assistant's document index lists every file the university links, with its year. The exam plan of the semester that has just ended (summer semester 2026) is available for most programmes.

notes: Written from what the university site showed on 2026-11-08.
title: Semester dates, lecture periods and exam periods (Semesterzeiten, Vorlesungszeit, Prüfungszeit)
content: The year is split into lecture periods (Vorlesungszeit), exam periods (Prüfungszeit) and lecture-free periods (vorlesungsfreie Zeit). The winter semester 2026/27 runs from 1 October 2026 to 14 March 2027; lectures run until 15 January 2027 and the first lecture day after the welcome day is Friday 2 October 2026. The page "Vorlesungs-, Prüfungs- und vorlesungsfreie Zeiten" gives the exact dates for each semester and can be subscribed to in a calendar app.
